cards.text: Jeremiah, a prophet in Judah, has been carrying the LORD's hard words to Judah's kings. One of them, Coniah, just heard that none of his descendants will sit on the throne of David (Jeremiah 22:30). Now the LORD declares woe on the shepherds.

cards.question: Shepherds are supposed to look after sheep. What does the LORD say these shepherds are doing to the sheep instead?
The LORD calls these sheep the shepherds' own flock.

cards.text: The LORD says it plain: they scattered His flock, drove them away and didn't attend to them. Friend, I've dropped a cookie or two packing a box, but these guys lost the WHOLE flock.

cards.question: The shepherds never attended to the LORD's flock. So who does the LORD say He'll attend to for the evil of their deeds?

cards.text: They skipped attending, and now THEY get attended to. That is not the kind of attention you want, but the LORD has a plan for the remnant of His flock, scattered across the lands.

cards.question: Somebody has to go get the remnant of the LORD's flock. Who does the LORD say will gather them?
The LORD says He Himself banished His flock to the lands He'll gather them from.

cards.text: He brings them back to their pasture, where they'll be fruitful and multiply. Then He takes care of the shepherd problem.

cards.question: What does the LORD say He'll raise up over His gathered flock?
Under the new shepherds, the LORD says a few of His sheep will still go missing.

cards.text: No more fear, no more dismay, and not ONE sheep missing. Friend, I can't keep track of my own oven timer, and then the LORD says, "Behold, the days are coming."

cards.question: Coniah's descendants won't sit on David's throne. But the LORD says He will raise up a righteous Branch for ___.
What does the LORD say this righteous Branch will do?

cards.text: And He will administer justice and righteousness in the land. FINALLY. A King who actually reads the whole job description.

cards.question: In the Branch's days, Judah will be ___ and Israel will dwell ___.
The LORD gives the righteous Branch a name. What will He be called?

cards.text: Then the LORD says the days are coming when people will stop saying, "As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the Israelites up out of the land of Egypt." Something's coming so big it bumps THAT off the top of the playlist.

cards.question: So when people say "As surely as the LORD lives," what rescue will they name instead of Egypt?

answers.text: Bringing them back from the north

cards.text: From the land of the north and every land He banished them to, the LORD leads them up, and they dwell once more in their own land. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me: "once more in their own land" is the best line in the whole thing.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 12 quotes "Behold, the days are coming.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says Jeremiah 'has been carrying the LORD's hard words to Judah's kings.' That is a Bible fact from outside the passage, and it has no reference. Only the Coniah line is cited (Jeremiah 22:30).

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The joke compares the shepherds to Papa Dorin accidentally dropping a cookie, and says they 'lost' the flock. In the text, the shepherds destroy, scatter and drive away the sheep (Jeremiah 23:1-2). That is deliberate harm, not a clumsy accident, so the comparison doesn't have the same core action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question says the shepherds 'never attended' to the flock. Jeremiah 23:2 says they 'have not attended to them.' 'Never' pushes the text further than it goes, and this isn't in one of Papa Dorin's jokes.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The oven-timer joke and the LORD's next words run together in one sentence: 'I can't keep track of my own oven timer, and then the LORD says, "Behold, the days are coming."' This blends the joke with the Bible setting. It reads as if the LORD's words answer the joke, and a stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The question says 'Coniah's descendants won't sit on David's throne. But the LORD says...' This presents the Branch as an answer to Coniah's line. Jeremiah 23:5 never mentions Coniah, so the card adds a connection the text leaves open. Putting 'David's throne' right before the blank also makes 'David' obvious and rules out Moses and Saul.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The setup inside the question ('Coniah's descendants won't sit on David's throne') points straight at 'David' and rules out the wrong answers 'Moses' and 'Saul.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke 'A King who actually reads the whole job description' is aimed at the righteous Branch, the coming King called The LORD Our Righteousness. It treats Him as an employee clearing a low bar. The humor should stay on the failed shepherds, not on the Branch.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: The right answers ('saved', 'securely') are hopeful words. All three wrong answers ('scattered', 'banished', 'abroad') are words of exile, which clash with the hopeful context. The right answers stand out by tone. Only 'abroad' could fit the second blank next to 'securely', so that blank becomes a two-way pick.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Saving them from the Assyrians' is close to the right answer, 'Bringing them back from the north.' Assyria was a northern power that carried Israel away, so a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
